key_insight: Lost on Campus introduces a benchmark for testing whether vision-language models can reason about space in large-scale, real-world outdoor 3D environments. It targets abilities that static-image and synthetic indoor tests may not faithfully measure.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks can reward semantic shortcuts rather than genuine embodied spatial reasoning, leaving uncertainty about model capabilities in real-world settings.
method: Introduce Lost on Campus as a benchmark focused on embodied spatial reasoning.
Evaluate spatial reasoning in large-scale, real-world outdoor 3D environments rather than only static images or synthetic indoor scenes.
The provided abstract is truncated, so specific tasks, metrics, and evaluation results are not available.
impact: The benchmark could help practitioners assess spatial reasoning under more realistic conditions before deploying vision-language models in embodied applications. The provided excerpt does not establish how current models perform.

paper_title: Lost on Campus: Evaluating Embodied Spatial Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in the Wild
paper_authors: Zehan Zheng, Yanyuan Chen, Deming Li, Yutao Tang, Jianwen Xie
